Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.sqlite

Class SQLiteSchemaGrammar

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.grammar.SchemaGrammar
org.aristonis.diwan.database.sqlite.SQLiteSchemaGrammar
public class SQLiteSchemaGrammar extends SchemaGrammar
Writes SQLite SQL, following Laravel's SQLiteGrammar.

SQLite has no unsigned types and no column comments, so unsigned() and comment() are ignored, as in Laravel. JSON is stored as text. An auto-increment column becomes integer primary key autoincrement, which SQLite allows only when the table is created.

Adding or dropping a primary or foreign key on an existing table rebuilds it, keeping its rows, indexes and auto-increment counter; tables with features the rebuild cannot carry over, such as CHECK constraints, triggers or generated columns, are refused instead. Renaming and dropping columns run in place on SQLite 3.25 and 3.35 and later, and rebuild the table on older versions.

Instances hold no state and are safe to share between threads.

    • compile

      public List<String> compile(Blueprint blueprint, Connection connection)
      Compiles every command of a blueprint.
      Overrides:
      compile in class SchemaGrammar
      Parameters:
      blueprint - the checked blueprint, never null
      connection - the connection the SQL will run on, never null; a grammar may read the current schema through it
      Returns:
      the statements in the order to run them, unmodifiable, never null
      Implementation Note:
      A blueprint that changes keys, drops or renames columns or renames an index on an existing table is compiled against the table's current shape, read through connection; when SQLite cannot make a change in place, the table is rebuilt: a new table, the rows copied, the old one dropped, the new one renamed, the indexes and the auto-increment counter restored.

    • withoutForeignKeyConstraints

      public <T> T withoutForeignKeyConstraints(Connection connection, TransactionCallback<T> work)
      Runs work in one transaction with foreign key enforcement switched off, as Laravel's withoutForeignKeyConstraints does.
      Overrides:
      withoutForeignKeyConstraints in class SchemaGrammar
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the result
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection, never null, outside any transaction
      work - the work, never null
      Returns:
      the result of the work, may be null
      Implementation Note:
      Holds one physical connection, switches PRAGMA foreign_keys off before the transaction starts, since SQLite ignores the switch inside one, and switches it back on after the transaction ends. If switching it back fails, the work stays committed and the session is discarded: a driver that can abort the connection makes the pool drop it.

    • sortForDrop

      public List<TableInfo> sortForDrop(Connection connection, List<TableInfo> tables)
      Orders the tables so that dropping them one after the other respects foreign keys.
      Overrides:
      sortForDrop in class SchemaGrammar
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection the tables were listed on, never null
      tables - the tables to drop, never null
      Returns:
      the tables, each before the listed tables it refers to, read from the foreign keys; the input order if they refer to each other in a cycle, where the deferred checks of compileDropAllTables(java.util.List<org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.TableInfo>) carry the drop. A RESTRICT action is not deferred, so the order is what lets such a schema drop

    • compileDropAllTables

      public List<String> compileDropAllTables(List<TableInfo> tables)
      Returns the statements that drop the given tables.

      More than one statement means they must run together in one transaction.

      Overrides:
      compileDropAllTables in class SchemaGrammar
      Parameters:
      tables - the tables to drop, never null, as listed by SchemaGrammar.compileTables(org.aristonis.diwan.database.Connection)
      Returns:
      PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = ON and one drop table per table. The pragma works inside a transaction and resets when it ends, so the statements must run in one; the schema builder does so. A foreign key whose action is RESTRICT still stops the drop of a table that rows refer to
